newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally at close on S&P, Dow.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally at close on S&P, Dow.

text.p: Argentine stocks woke abruptly from their slumber and surged at the close Tuesday, powered by Standard & Poor's upgrade of five bank foreign currency counterparty ratings and the Dow's second-largest point gain in history, dealers said.

"The main factor driving the market at the close were the S&P upgrades, including three which placed the debt of the institutions involved at investment grade or higher than the sovereign debt rating," a trader at a large local bank said.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV jumped 2.4 percent to 714.77, trailing a 2.6 percent leap by the Dow.

"We didn't expect this rally in the Dow today, although in hindsight it's logical because it underscores the pattern of strong economic growth with low inflation (in the United States)," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli, noting quarterly results of leading Wall Street companies came in better than expected.

But the bolsa got a special boost from the S&P upgrades, which pushed the foreign currency counterparty ratings of Banco Rio, Banco Frances and Caja de Valores up to BBB- from BB, and those of Banco de Galicia and Mercado de Valores to BB+ from BB.
S&P had raised Argentina's sovereign debt to BB from BB- in the first days of April.
The Argentine market was also favored Tuesday by a Latin American portfolio shuffle by CS First Boston, which raised its Argentine holdings to overweight from neutral.

"With all this good news the bolsa should embark on a steady upward course tomorrow, when it digests all the implications," another trader said. He noted corporate financing costs would fall as a result of the bank rating upgrades.
The broad market index closed up 2.3 percent Tuesday, with winners pounding losers 50 to eight and 17 issues closed flat.
Floor volume nearly doubled to 29.9 million pesos Tuesday from 15.5 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 86.4 million pesos.
Top main-tier performers were electricity company Central Costanera, construction stock Polledo and Banco Frances, which shot up 5.0 percent, 4.7 percent and 4.1 percent, respectively.
Telefonica rose 4.0 percent, steelmaker Acindar 3.6 percent and petrochemical concern Indupa 3.1 percent.
The only MerVal loser was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which tumbled 9.2 percent on earnings jitters, dealers said.
